newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court keeps Commission banana rules on Ivory Coast imports.
newsitem.headline: Court keeps Commission banana rules on Ivory Coast imports.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance dismissed on Wednesday a plea to throw out European Commission rules limiting imports of bananas from the Ivory Coast into the European Union.

The importers told the court the Commission's adoption of new rules in 1994 severely limited their import allowance of Ivory Coast bananas, from 35,000 tonnes to 5,250 tonnes, fundamentally altering earlier entitlements.

The court rejected the argument of direct and individual concern finding instead that the Commission regulation "affects every importer wishing to import bananas from the Ivory Coast and the fact that the applicants currently import a large proportion of Ivory Coast bananas does not amount to circumstances differentiating them from other importers."

The court found the regulation affects the importers only indirectly as the import licences are issued by the member states. "Only the decisions of the member states granting or refusing such licences are capable of concerning the applicants directly," the court said.
